title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act establishes guidelines to ensure that artificial‑intelligence tools used in processing veterans’ claims are transparent, unbiased, and regularly reviewed. It aims to protect veterans by holding the VA responsible for how AI decisions influence claim outcomes.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to publicly disclose how it uses artificial intelligence, including details on data sources, algorithms, and decision‑making processes. The law aims to enhance accountability, protect veterans’ privacy, and let stakeholders review the fairness and safety of AI‑driven services.

title: To establish age-appropriate design standards and safety safeguards for artificial intelligence chatbots accessed by minors, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy establishes guidelines to ensure that artificial‑intelligence chatbots used by children are designed with age‑appropriate content and safety features. It also sets safety safeguards for other applications of AI chatbots to protect all users.

title: To prohibit Chinese AI models from being used on government-issued devices or software systems, to prohibit the procurement of any such models, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The policy bars the use of Chinese AI models on any government‑issued devices or software systems and prohibits the government from purchasing these models. It also includes additional restrictions to ensure that no Chinese AI technology is employed or acquired by public sector entities.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act proposes a nationwide campaign to increase public understanding of AI technologies. It will fund educational programs, informational resources, and public outreach so citizens are informed about AI benefits and risks.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for systematically assessing the risks posed by AI systems. It requires entities to conduct risk evaluations, report findings to regulators, and implement mitigation measures to ensure safe and responsible AI deployment.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee AI policy, research, and regulation. It outlines the committee’s purpose, membership, and mandate to guide responsible AI development and address potential risks.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that sets out rules and guidelines for developing and using artificial intelligence. It aims to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with societal values by requiring compliance with standards and oversight from regulatory bodies.

title: A bill to require the Secretary of Defense to establish reporting requirements and voluntary guidance for large artificial intelligence contractors.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill requires the Secretary of Defense to set up reporting requirements for large artificial intelligence contractors, ensuring the government can monitor their activities and compliance. It also calls for voluntary guidance to help those contractors align with defense standards and best practices.

title: A bill to provide for the retraining and support of workers displaced by automation technologies or artificial intelligence, to require Federal action during periods of elevated unemployment, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The bill proposes federal programs to retrain and support workers displaced by automation or artificial intelligence. It also requires federal action during periods of elevated unemployment and includes additional related measures.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate resolution stresses that religious freedom is essential and that authoritative texts should be respected in public life. It also calls for greater transparency in the design and deployment of artificial‑intelligence systems.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes to create the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, a new agency that would monitor the safety of AI technologies and advise policymakers. The bill also includes other related measures to strengthen AI regulation and oversight.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a new law designed to safeguard people from misleading or unfair use of artificial intelligence in everyday products and services. It sets out rules for clear labeling, honest disclosure of AI involvement, and penalties for companies that trick consumers with deceptive AI practices.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 sets out national standards to ensure that new AI systems are safe, reliable, and transparent before they are released to the public. It requires developers to conduct thorough safety testing, disclose design choices, and establish oversight mechanisms to protect users and promote trustworthy AI innovation.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress detailing how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of FISA. The report will examine AI’s role in surveillance operations and its impact on privacy and national security.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to improve AI knowledge and job readiness by providing educational resources, training programs, and workforce development initiatives across schools and industries. It aims to ensure that students and employees are equipped with the skills and knowledge needed for emerging AI careers and to support a future‑ready workforce.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is intended to foster open‑source development and leadership in AI technology. It encourages collaboration, transparency, and equitable access to AI tools and resources.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 requires that all medical diagnoses, treatments, and patient care decisions be made by licensed physicians rather than artificial‑intelligence systems, ensuring clear accountability and safeguarding patient safety. It imposes penalties on healthcare providers who use AI for clinical decisions without appropriate human oversight and mandates strict regulatory oversight of any AI tools used in medical settings.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is designed to stop businesses from using artificial intelligence to charge excessively high prices for services and to manipulate workers’ wages through automated systems. It would set rules and penalties to promote fair pricing and protect employees from AI-driven wage exploitation.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and investigate incidents related to cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. The board would also be tasked with other duties aimed at ensuring the safe and responsible use of AI technology.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The bill proposes creating the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund to finance research, development, and deployment of AI technologies, ensuring the U.S. stays competitive and addresses societal impacts. It also sets up oversight mechanisms, allocates funds to key areas, and encourages collaboration between government, academia, and industry to promote responsible AI use.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act establishes guidelines for developing and deploying AI models, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and safety. It requires companies to disclose model data, use‑case limitations, and potential biases, and sets up oversight mechanisms to monitor compliance.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act seeks to shield households from the rising energy bills driven by large AI data centers. It proposes limits on the energy usage of these centers and provides financial relief or subsidies to families affected by the increased costs.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act creates a federal department dedicated to fostering research, development, and deployment of advanced AI technologies. It sets out regulatory standards, funding priorities, and ethical guidelines to ensure responsible innovation and protect public interests.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 establishes rules to make sure AI tools used by the Department of Veterans Affairs are safe, fair, and respect veterans’ privacy. It creates oversight, sets clear guidelines, and requires that AI systems be transparent and regularly reviewed to protect veterans from bias, errors, or misuse.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is proposed legislation designed to curb the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems that pose significant societal risks. It aims to enforce stricter oversight and accountability measures to prevent autonomous AI from acting independently in ways that could cause harm.
